Laboratory.cell: Pheasant Memorial Laboratory (PML) for Geochemistry and Cosmochemistry, Okayama University (affiliation)
Laboratory.value: Pheasant Memorial Laboratory (PML) for Geochemistry and Cosmochemistry, Okayama University (affiliation)

Procedure Reference(s).cell: Makishima and Nakamura (2006) — 'Details of these methods and ICP operating conditions are described in Makishima and Nakamura (2006)'

Target Material.cell: basalt; andesite; peridotite; dunite; synthetic glass; carbonaceous chondrite — GSJ and USGS silicate RMs, NIST SRM 610–616 glasses, and Orgueil, Murchison and Allende

Sampling Unit Type.cell: Test portion / solution aliquot -- "The amount of test portion used was 15-42 mg for basalt and andesite samples, and 30-63 mg for peridotite samples"; NIST glasses "a few grains totalling 8-22 mg were used in one analysis"; "the same sample solution aliquot"
Sampling Unit Type.value: Test portion / solution aliquot -- "The amount of test portion used was 15-42 mg for basalt and andesite samples, and 30-63 mg for peridotite samples"; NIST glasses "a few grains totalling 8-22 mg were used in one analysis"; "the same sample solution aliquot"

Sample Preparation Method.cell: Rock powders decomposed with the Sm spike; NIST glasses crushed roughly in a silicon nitride mortar, chips hand-picked, washed and dried; solutions diluted with 0.5 mol/l HNO3 to a dilution factor ≥ 1000 — clean room at PML; NIST SRM 610 decomposed without spike, the Sm spike added to its solution
Sample Preparation Method.value: Rock powders decomposed with the Sm spike; NIST glasses crushed roughly in a silicon nitride mortar, chips hand-picked, washed and dried; solutions diluted with 0.5 mol/l HNO3 to a dilution factor ≥ 1000

Digestion Acid(s).cell: ultrasonic HF-HClO4: HF + HClO4; bomb HF: HF; HClO4 drying: HClO4; final uptake: 0.5 mol/l HNO3

Digestion Vessel Type.cell: TFE bomb for peridotites and chondrites — the vessel for the ultrasonic digestion is not stated
Digestion Vessel Type.value: TFE bomb for peridotites and chondrites

Digestion Step.cell: ultrasonic HF-HClO4 (basalts, andesites and NIST SRM 612, 614, 616, with the Sm spike, in an ultrasonic bath, dried to decompose fluorides); bomb HF (peridotites and chondrites, with the Sm spike, in a TFE bomb at 245 °C); HClO4 drying (the bomb digests); final uptake (0.5 mol/l HNO3) — after Yokoyama et al. (1999) and Makishima and Nakamura (2006)

Final Solution Matrix.cell: all: 0.5 mol/l HNO3, dilution factor ≥ 1000 — the same acid for calibrator, sample and washout solutions

Sample Aliquot Mass or Volume.cell: 15–42 mg (basalts and andesites); 30–63 mg (peridotites); 8–22 mg (NIST glasses); 9–28 mg (chondrites)
Sample Aliquot Mass or Volume.value: 15–42 mg (basalts and andesites); 30–63 mg (peridotites); 8–22 mg (NIST glasses); 9–28 mg (chondrites)

Isotope Dilution Spike.cell: 149Sm-enriched spike — for the ID of Sm, whose ¹⁴⁹Sm intensity is the internal standard for Cd, In, Tl and Bi

Instrument Manufacturer.cell: Agilent -- "Agilent 7500cs; Yokogawa Analytical Systems, Mitaka, Japan"
Instrument Manufacturer.value: Agilent -- "Agilent 7500cs; Yokogawa Analytical Systems, Mitaka, Japan"

Analytical Mode.cell: Flow injection -- "The pseudo-flow injection (FI) sample introduction technique, in which transient signals were integrated as total counts, was employed with the ID-IS method to minimise total sample consumption volume (~0.013 ml)"
Analytical Mode.value: Flow injection -- "The pseudo-flow injection (FI) sample introduction technique, in which transient signals were integrated as total counts, was employed with the ID-IS method to minimise total sample consumption volume (~0.013 ml)"

Target Species.cell: Cd, In, Tl, Bi — Sm is determined by ID as the internal standard

Reported Variables and Units.cell: Cd, In, Tl, Bi (µg/g) — Tables 3–5; detection limits in pg/ml and ng/g

Monitored Masses.key: defines: monitored property per target species
Monitored Masses.cell: 111Cd → Cd; 115In → In; 205Tl → Tl; 209Bi → Bi; 95Mo, 113Cd, 118Sn, 149Sm → none — Table 1; '113Cd was not used for Cd determination, because the correction of 113In was far larger than the MoO correction'

Analysis Sequence.cell: Multi-element standard solution after every third sample, Mo standard solution after every sixth sample — each measurement ~6 min, including ~200 s wash
Analysis Sequence.value: Multi-element standard solution after every third sample, Mo standard solution after every sixth sample

Wash Time Between Samples.cell: ~200 s with 0.5 mol/l HNO3 — 0.5 mol/l HF aspirated for 200 s after the Mo standard

Internal Standard Concentration.cell: N — Sm at 1.22 ng/ml in the calibrator

Oxide Production Method and Threshold.cell: CeO+/Ce+ < 0.01 under the operating conditions — MoO+/Mo+ from a Mo standard every sixth sample, 0.8–7.4 × 10⁻⁴ during the study

Drift Correction Method.cell: Mass discrimination corrected with the mean elemental ratios of the calibrator measured before and after each sample — step (d)
Drift Correction Method.value: Mass discrimination corrected with the mean elemental ratios of the calibrator measured before and after each sample

Calibration Strategy per Target Species.cell: Cd, In, Tl, Bi: isotope dilution–internal standardisation (ID-IS) against 149Sm — Eq. 2; Sm by isotope dilution (Eq. 1)

Spectral Interference Corrections Applie.cell: Y — MoO⁺ on ¹¹¹Cd, ¹¹⁵Sn on ¹¹⁵In; ⁷¹Ga⁴⁰Ar⁺ on ¹¹¹Cd < 0.3%, negligible

Interference Correction Method.cell: 111Cd: (95MoO+ + 94MoOH+) subtracted using the mean MoO+/Mo+ of the Mo standard measured before and after the sample; 115In: isobaric correction with 115Sn/118Sn = 0.014; 113Cd: net 113In with 113In/115In = 0.0448; other: N — steps (b)–(c)

value.value: (95MoO+ + 94MoOH+) subtracted using the mean MoO+/Mo+ of the Mo standard measured before and after the sample

Isotope Dilution Data Reduction Method.cell: Eq. 1 for Sm (ID), with the pseudo-concentration Q calibrated on spike-standard mixtures, and Eq. 2 for Cd, In, Tl and Bi (ID-IS) — details in Makishima and Nakamura (2006)
Isotope Dilution Data Reduction Method.value: Eq. 1 for Sm (ID), with the pseudo-concentration Q calibrated on spike-standard mixtures, and Eq. 2 for Cd, In, Tl and Bi (ID-IS)

Memory Effect Mitigation.cell: ~200 s wash with 0.5 mol/l HNO3, and 200 s with 0.5 mol/l HF after the Mo standard, since Mo was difficult to wash out with HNO3
Memory Effect Mitigation.value: ~200 s wash with 0.5 mol/l HNO3, and 200 s with 0.5 mol/l HF after the Mo standard, since Mo was difficult to wash out with HNO3

Uncertainty Level.cell: RSD% (n = 5) and RPD (relative percentage difference) -- both used; "RPD, relative percentage difference"
Uncertainty Level.value: RSD% (n = 5) and RPD (relative percentage difference) -- both used; "RPD, relative percentage difference"

Uncertainty Propagation Method.cell: Cd: total uncertainty estimated < 7%, from matrix and oxide errors (< 3% and < 5%) and an intermediate precision of 3%; other: N

value.value: total uncertainty estimated < 7%, from matrix and oxide errors (< 3% and < 5%) and an intermediate precision of 3%

Calibration Factor and Determination Met.cell: Cd, In, Tl, Bi: relative concentration factor f_G against Sm, from the calibrator measured before and after the sample — Eq. 2

value.value: relative concentration factor f_G against Sm, from the calibrator measured before and after the sample

Analysis Inclusion and Rejection Criteri.cell: Partially -- n = 5 (evaporation test), n = 4 (dissolution blanks), "an average of eight sessions" for detection limits. No acceptance or rejection rule for individual results is stated. The 113Cd decision is a mass-selection decision, not an aggregation one, and is recorded under Monitored Masses
Analysis Inclusion and Rejection Criteri.value: Partially -- n = 5 (evaporation test), n = 4 (dissolution blanks), "an average of eight sessions" for detection limits. No acceptance or rejection rule for individual results is stated. The 113Cd decision is a mass-selection decision, not an aggregation one, and is recorded under Monitored Masses

Combination Method.cell: all: average over repeat measurements — evaporation-test ratios 'together with the RSD (n = 5)'; detection limits 'an average of eight sessions'

Constants and Reference Values Used.cell: 115Sn/118Sn = 0.014 and 113In/115In = 0.0448 (Rosman and Taylor 1998); 94Mo/95Mo = 0.58; MoOH+/MoO+ ~0.15 (measured); 111Cd/113Cd = 1.05 as reference
Constants and Reference Values Used.value: 115Sn/118Sn = 0.014 and 113In/115In = 0.0448 (Rosman and Taylor 1998); 94Mo/95Mo = 0.58; MoOH+/MoO+ ~0.15 (measured); 111Cd/113Cd = 1.05 as reference

Primary Calibration Standard Name.cell: all [Cd, Tl, Bi: multi-element standard solution, 0.110 ng/ml; In: the same solution, 0.111 ng/ml] — with Sm at 1.22 ng/ml

Secondary Reference Materials.cell: JB-2, JB-3, JA-1, JA-2, JA-3, JP-1, BHVO-1, AGV-1, PCC-1, DTS-1, NIST SRM 610, NIST SRM 612, NIST SRM 614, NIST SRM 616 — the chondrites are samples

Detection Limit.cell: Cd: 0.8; In: 0.2; Tl: 0.9; Bi: 0.2 — 3s, in pg/ml in solution and in ng/g in silicates at DF 1000 (Table 1)

Detection Limit Method.cell: all: 3s of the background signal of 0.5 mol/l HNO3, average of eight sessions — Results

value.value: 3s of the background signal of 0.5 mol/l HNO3, average of eight sessions

Counting Statistics Error.key: sample > sampling unit x reported property

Internal (Within-Measurement) Analytical.key: sample > sampling unit x reported property

Within-Session Analytical Precision and.cell: all [Cd: 2.0%; In, Tl, Bi: 1.6%] — RPD of X/¹⁴⁹Sm between neighbouring calibrator runs (Table 1)

Between-Session (Long-Term) Analytical P.cell: JB-2, JB-3, JA-1, JA-2, JA-3, BHVO-1, AGV-1 [Cd: 3–10%]; JP-1, PCC-1, DTS-1 [Cd: 7–16%]; NIST SRM 610, NIST SRM 612, NIST SRM 614, NIST SRM 616 [Cd: 2–3%; In: 0.7–3%; Tl: 6–12%; Bi: 1–4%] — intermediate precision, RSD of n = 4–8 separate decompositions (Tables 3 and 4)

Analytical Accuracy and Assessment Metho.cell: JB-2, JB-3, JA-1, JA-2, JA-3 [Cd: broadly similar to the reference values of Govindaraju (1994) and Imai et al. (1995)]; BHVO-1, AGV-1 [Cd: differ from those reference values] — Table 3; In, Tl and Bi compared with previous studies

value.value: broadly similar to the reference values of Govindaraju (1994) and Imai et al. (1995)

Additional Notes.cell: ICP operating conditions as in Makishima and Nakamura (2006); pseudo-flow injection with transient signals integrated as total counts, ~0.013 ml per measurement; an evaporation test showed no loss of Cd, In, Tl or Bi (ratios 0.996–0.999, Table 2)
Additional Notes.value: ICP operating conditions as in Makishima and Nakamura (2006); pseudo-flow injection with transient signals integrated as total counts, ~0.013 ml per measurement; an evaporation test showed no loss of Cd, In, Tl or Bi (ratios 0.996–0.999, Table 2)
